question: What should you do at an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a: Maintain speed and proceed.,b: Slow down, be prepared to stop, check all directions, and yield as needed.,c: Yield to all other drivers.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must slow and be prepared to stop, look carefully in all directions, and yield to any traffic already in the intersection or approaching closely—especially vehicles coming from your right. A full stop is required only if needed for safety or to yield the right‑of‑way.

question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:
options: a: Drivers already in the intersection, b: Oncoming traffic, c: Pedestrians in the intersection, d: All of the above
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, to pedestrians in the crosswalk or intersection, and to any vehicles or cyclists already in the intersection. Turn only when the way is completely clear.

question: Which vehicle must yield when two vehicles enter an intersection simultaneously from different roads?
options: a: Either vehicle.,b: The vehicle on the left.,c: The vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive simultaneously with a vehicle to your right, you should:
options: a: Speed through the intersection., b: Yield to the vehicle on the right., c: Enter and force the other vehicle to stop.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Yielding to the vehicle on your right helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: At a four-way stop:
options: a: The first vehicle to arrive has the right-of-way, b: The last vehicle to arrive has the right-of-way, c: One driver may proceed without stopping
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first and comes to a complete stop has the right-of-way and may proceed first. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. Always proceed with caution and be prepared to yield if another driver does something unexpected.

question: When approaching an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must:
options: a: Slow down and change lanes if possible, b: Drive to the right and stop, c: Maintain speed in your lane
note: Move Over laws require you to slow down and, if it is safe and legal, change lanes away from a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. If you cannot change lanes, reduce your speed significantly and pass with extra caution, giving as much space as possible.

question: What must you do when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a: Change lanes or slow down.,b: Drive to the right and stop.,c: Continue at the same speed.
note: Change lanes away from a stopped emergency vehicle or slow down if unable to move over, giving it space.

question: What must you do on a narrow road with an oncoming vehicle?
options: a: Pull completely off the road.,b: Allow the oncoming vehicle half the road.,c: Demand the other vehicle pull over.
note: On a narrow road, you must allow oncoming traffic at least half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway. Slow down, keep as far to the right as is safe, and share the available space so both vehicles can pass without leaving the roadway or creating a hazard.

question: What should you do if you hear a siren behind you on the roadway?
options: a: Stop where you are., b: Pull over to the right and stop., c: Speed up to clear the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from behind, safely move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. This creates a clear lane so the emergency vehicle can get through quickly and safely.

question: What should you do while waiting to turn left in an intersection?
options: a: Signal and keep wheels turned left.,b: Signal and keep wheels straight.,c: Flash headlights to signal drivers.
note: When waiting to turn left, signal early and keep your wheels straight while you are stopped in the intersection. If you are rear-ended with your wheels turned left, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic; straight wheels help you be pushed forward instead.

question: When hearing a siren behind you on the road, you should:
options: a: Stop where you are, b: Pull over to the right and stop, c: Speed up to clear the way
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: You must pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle:
options: a: When it is approaching from ahead or behind on your side of the road., b: Only if it’s following you, c: Not when it is separated from you by a physical median or barrier on a divided highway
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren on, you must immediately pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, unless you are in an intersection. This applies whether the vehicle is coming from ahead or behind on the same roadway. You are not required to stop for emergency vehicles that are on the opposite side of a divided highway or median, because they cannot cross into your lanes.

question: Who has the right-of-way at an uncontrolled intersection when two vehicles arrive simultaneously?
options: a: The vehicle on the right.,b: The vehicle on the left.,c: The vehicle that honks first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right goes first. Honking does not give a driver the right-of-way.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a: Never., b: When they use flashing lights and siren (or emergency signals)., c: Only if other vehicles yield.
note: You must immediately yield the right‑of‑way to emergency vehicles that are using both their flashing lights and siren (or, in some states, at least their lights). Safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by an officer.

question: What should you do when preparing to turn left?
options: a: Slow down and check your rearview mirror.,b: Move into the left lane.,c: Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: When preparing to turn left, you must signal, move into the proper lane, slow as needed, and most importantly yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Watching carefully for oncoming traffic and people in the crosswalk is critical because they have the right-of-way when you are turning left.

question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which must yield?
options: a: Either vehicle, b: The vehicle on the left, c: The vehicle on the right
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, which has the right-of-way?
options: a: The vehicle on the right, b: The vehicle on the left, c: The vehicle sounding its horn first
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions by clearly assigning priority.

question: A driver entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp:
options: a: Must yield to vehicles already on the interstate, b: Has the right-of-way, c: Can force their way into traffic
note: A driver entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp must yield to traffic already on the highway. Use the ramp to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Vehicles on the interstate are not required to change lanes or slow down to let you in, although they may do so as a courtesy.

question: What should you do if stopped in a line at a stop sign with no cross traffic after others pass?
options: a: Proceed without stopping again.,b: Stop again at the stop sign.,c: Roll past the stop sign slowly.
note: Always stop completely at a stop sign, even in a line of traffic, to yield to any approaching vehicles.

question: What should you avoid when making a right turn?
options: a: Signaling to other drivers.,b: Swinging too wide.,c: Slowing down.
note: When making a right turn, you should stay close to the right curb and turn into the right lane of the road you are entering. Swinging too wide can put you into another lane or into the path of oncoming or adjacent traffic, increasing the risk of a collision. Always signal and slow down appropriately before turning.

question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:
options: a: Never, b: When they use flashing lights or sirens, c: Only when other vehicles yield
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles that are using their siren and/or flashing lights. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: What should you do when faced with an oncoming car and a bicyclist on a narrow road?
options: a: Pull onto the shoulder.,b: Split the difference.,c: Let the car pass before passing the bike.
note: On a narrow road with oncoming traffic and a bicyclist, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, then move over safely to pass the bicyclist when you have enough space.

question: When being tailgated:
options: a: Move to the right if possible, b: Slow down gradually when clear to encourage passing, c: Avoid abrupt slowing, d: All of the above
note: When someone is following too closely, you should create a safer situation for yourself and others. If possible, move to the right so the tailgater can pass. If you need to adjust your speed, slow down gradually when the way is clear so they are encouraged to go around you. Avoid sudden braking or abrupt slowing, which can cause a rear‑end collision.

question: When hearing or seeing an emergency vehicle approaching, you should:
options: a: Stop immediately, b: Drive to the right and stop, c: Proceed slowly to let it pass
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop, if it is safe to do so. Stopping on the right creates a clear path in the center or left for the emergency vehicle to pass quickly and safely. Continue only after it has passed and the way is clear.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with sirens or lights approaches?
options: a: Pull to the right and stop.,b: Pull to the right and slow down.,c: Pull to the right and use four-way flashers.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens or flashing lights approaches from any direction, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: What should you do when wanting to turn left at an intersection with heavy oncoming traffic?
options: a: Use the next intersection.,b: Wait at the crosswalk.,c: Wait in the intersection’s center.
note: When turning left with a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you typically pull into the intersection, keep your wheels straight, and wait for a safe gap to complete the turn. Keeping the wheels straight helps prevent being pushed into oncoming traffic if you are hit from behind. In some states, however, you are required to wait behind the stop line until you can complete the turn, so always follow your state’s specific rules.

question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:
options: a: Has the right-of-way, b: Must yield to drivers on the public road, c: Can force their way into traffic
note: A driver entering a public road from a driveway, alley, or private road must yield to all traffic and pedestrians already on the public road. You may enter only when it is safe and will not force others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: What should you do when a traffic light turns green?
options: a: Yield to pedestrians still in the intersection.,b: Accelerate quickly.,c: Back up slowly.
note: When a traffic light turns green, you may proceed only after making sure the intersection is clear and yielding to any pedestrians still in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. A green light means go if it is safe, not that you should accelerate quickly or move in reverse.

question: When turning onto a one-way street, drivers should:
options: a: Turn into the right lane.,b: Turn into the left lane.,c: Turn into the proper lane for your turn, usually the nearest available lane in your direction of travel.
note: When turning onto a one‑way street, you must turn into the lane that is legally required for your movement, usually the nearest available lane in the direction you are turning. This keeps traffic organized and predictable. You may then change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What should you do when approaching a T intersection?
options: a: Yield to cross traffic.,b: Proceed with the right-of-way.,c: Force your way into traffic.
note: At a T intersection, the driver on the road that ends must yield to traffic on the through road. You must wait until cross traffic is clear and it is safe before entering or crossing the intersection.

question: How should you merge onto a freeway?
options: a: Proceed slowly waiting for an opening., b: Use the ramp to accelerate to near freeway speed and merge when safe., c: Use hazard lights until merged.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, then merge when there is a safe gap, yielding to vehicles already on the freeway. Entering too slowly can force other drivers to brake or swerve, increasing the risk of a collision.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the main road after a stop, you must:
options: a: Honk to alert them, b: Move to the left lane, c: Yield
note: When a transit bus signals that it is pulling out from a stop back into the lane, you must yield and allow it to re-enter when it is safe. Slowing or stopping if needed helps the bus merge smoothly and protects passengers who are boarding or exiting.

question: When turning onto a one-way street, what should you do?
options: a: Always turn into the far right lane.,b: Always turn into the far left lane.,c: Turn into the nearest lane that allows you to merge safely and interferes least with other traffic.
note: When turning onto a one‑way street, you should enter the lane that allows you to merge smoothly and safely with traffic, usually the nearest available lane in your direction that causes the least disruption. This helps prevent sudden lane changes and conflicts with other vehicles.

question: What should you do when moving from the right lane to the left on a multilane highway?
options: a: Check your mirrors for traffic behind and beside you., b: Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot., c: Signal, check mirrors, and look over your left shoulder before moving., d: Change lanes if you do not see a car directly next to you.
note: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you must use all three checks: look in your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, signal your intention, and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot. Only move over when the lane is clear and it is safe.

question: When seeing a vehicle entering your lane from a freeway ramp, you should:
options: a: Maintain a steady speed and position, adjusting or changing lanes if safe to allow merging., b: Honk to force them to slow down., c: Ignore them because you always have priority.
note: On most freeways, through traffic has the right‑of‑way and is not required to leave its lane for merging vehicles. You should maintain a safe, steady speed so the merging driver can judge gaps accurately. If it is safe, you may change lanes or slightly adjust speed to help them merge smoothly, but you should not make sudden or unpredictable moves.

question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens or flashing lights approaches, you must:
options: a: Slow down until it passes, b: Drive to the right and stop, c: Signal for it to pass
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials.

question: Must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?
options: a: On most roads, yes, but not when the emergency vehicle is on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median., b: Only if it’s directly behind you in your lane., c: Only if it’s approaching from the opposite direction on a two-lane road.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches from any direction on a two-way road, you must pull over to the right edge and stop until it passes, unless directed otherwise by police. On divided highways with a physical median, you generally do not stop for emergency vehicles traveling on the opposite side, because they are separated from your lanes by the median.

question: On a narrow road meeting an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a: Pull off and stop.,b: Allow the oncoming vehicle half the road.,c: Demand the other vehicle pull over.
note: On very narrow roads where two vehicles cannot safely pass, the driver who has the better opportunity to pull off should do so and stop, allowing the oncoming vehicle to pass. You must not insist on taking half the road if there is not enough room for both vehicles to pass safely.

question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a: Speed up, b: Maintain your speed if it is safe and legal, c: Slow down slightly to create more space for the passing vehicle to return safely
note: When another driver wants to pass you, you should maintain your current speed and stay in your lane so the passing driver can judge gaps and complete the pass safely. Do not speed up or make sudden moves. If road or traffic conditions require it, you may slow slightly, but the primary rule is to hold a steady speed.

question: What should you do when entering a street from a driveway?
options: a: Drive slowly to clear a path.,b: Honk to alert others.,c: Stop and yield to traffic and pedestrians.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road. Only enter when it is safe and you will not force others to slow or stop.

question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?
options: a: Honk to warn other drivers.,b: Stop partially on the roadway to signal entry.,c: Yield to pedestrians and traffic.
note: When entering a roadway from a private road, driveway, or alley, you must stop if necessary and yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the main road. Traffic on the public roadway has priority, so you only enter when it is safe and will not force others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop:
options: a: The driver on the right has priority, b: The driver on the left has priority, c: One may proceed without stopping
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. The driver on the left must yield, which helps keep traffic moving in an orderly and predictable way.

question: What should you do if opposing traffic blocks your view while waiting to turn left?
options: a: Accelerate when the first lane clears.,b: Wait until all lanes are clear.,c: Wait for an oncoming driver’s signal.
note: When turning left across oncoming traffic, you must wait until there is a safe gap in all lanes you need to cross or enter. If your view is blocked, do not move into the intersection blindly or rely on another driver’s signal. Only start your turn when you can clearly see that all lanes are free of oncoming vehicles and it is safe to complete the turn.

question: To merge onto a crowded freeway, you should:
options: a: Use mirrors and check blind spots, b: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed, c: Yield to freeway traffic, d: All of the above
note: When merging onto a crowded freeway, you must use your mirrors and check blind spots, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of freeway traffic, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Freeway traffic has the right-of-way, so you adjust your speed and position to merge safely without forcing others to brake suddenly.

question: Who must you yield to when turning left?
options: a: Drivers already in the intersection., b: Oncoming traffic., c: Pedestrians in the intersection., d: Oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and drivers already in the intersection.
note: When turning left, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming traffic, pedestrians in the crosswalk, and any vehicles already in the intersection. You may only complete your turn when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: What should you do when a vehicle enters your lane from a freeway ramp?
options: a: Adjust your speed or change lanes if safe to make room., b: Honk to alert them., c: Ignore them as you have the right-of-way.
note: Vehicles entering a freeway must yield to traffic already on the freeway, but safe driving means you should help create a smooth, safe merge. When a vehicle is entering your lane from a ramp, you should, when possible, adjust your speed or change lanes to make room. This reduces the chance of sudden braking or side‑swipe collisions and keeps traffic flowing safely.

question: How should you merge into traffic on a crowded freeway?
options: a: Check mirrors and blind spots.,b: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed.,c: Yield to freeway traffic already on the road and merge when there is a safe gap.
note: Traffic already on the freeway has the right-of-way. When merging, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of freeway traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots, and then merge only when there is a safe gap, yielding to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a: When entering from a garage, alley, or driveway.,b: When they’re on your right at an unmarked intersection.,c: When turning on a green light without a green arrow.
note: You must yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a roadway from a garage, alley, or driveway because vehicles already on the road have the right-of-way. At an unmarked intersection, you yield to vehicles on your right, not your left. A green arrow gives you the right-of-way for that protected movement, though you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: When driving on a street and hearing a siren but not seeing the emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a: Keep driving until you see it, b: Pull to the curb and stop, c: Slow down and don’t stop
note: Pull over and stop to ensure the emergency vehicle can pass safely, even if its location is unclear.

question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:
options: a: Always stop before entering, b: Slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians, stopping if needed, c: Yield only to traffic on the left
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop, but you are not required to stop if the way is clear. You must yield the right‑of‑way to any traffic or pedestrians already in or close to the intersection, stopping only when necessary to avoid interfering with them.

question: A driver on a frontage road of a controlled-access highway must yield to a vehicle:
options: a: Entering the frontage road from the highway, b: Leaving the frontage road to enter the highway, c: Both scenarios
note: On a controlled‑access highway, vehicles already on the main lanes of the highway have the right‑of‑way. A driver on a frontage (service) road must yield to vehicles that are leaving the highway to enter the frontage road, because those vehicles are coming from the main traveled way. A driver on the frontage road does not automatically have to yield to vehicles that are entering the highway; those entering must yield to highway traffic.

question: When do you have the right-of-way when turning left?
options: a: On a solid green light, after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians., b: On a flashing yellow light, after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians., c: On a green arrow pointing left, because oncoming traffic must stop.
note: A green left-turn arrow is a protected signal that means oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you have a red light, so you have the right-of-way to turn left if the intersection is clear. A solid green or flashing yellow light for a left turn requires you to yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before turning, because they have the right-of-way in those situations.

question: What should you avoid when making a left turn?
options: a: Failing to signal to other drivers., b: Cutting the corner., c: Failing to slow down.
note: When turning left, you must turn into the correct lane without cutting across the center of the intersection or into oncoming lanes. Cutting the corner can put you into the path of oncoming traffic or vehicles turning from the opposite direction. You should always signal before turning and slow down to a safe turning speed.

question: When completing a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, your car should end in:
options: a: The right lane, b: The center of the street, c: The left lane
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the leftmost lane that is going in your direction. This keeps you in the lane closest to the center line and avoids cutting across lanes, which can cause conflicts with other vehicles.

question: Which light indicates to slow down and proceed cautiously at an intersection?
options: a: Flashing yellow light.,b: Flashing red light.,c: Solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with extra caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles if needed.

question: What does a broken yellow line on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a: You’re on a two-way road.,b: You’re on a one-way road.,c: The road is under repair.
note: A broken yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions on a two-way road. It also means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so, because traffic from the other direction is using the opposite side of the center line.

question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a: Slow down.,b: Look for trains.,c: Be prepared to stop.,d: All of the above.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, you should slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Never assume the tracks are clear, and be especially cautious if visibility is limited or warning devices are active.

question: At a railroad crossing, you must stop:
options: a: If a stop sign is posted, b: If a crossing gate is lowered, c: If crossing lights are flashing, d: All of the above
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when there is a stop sign, when the gate is lowered or lowering, or when the red warning lights are flashing. These controls indicate a possible or approaching train, and stopping prevents you from entering the tracks when it is unsafe.

question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n:
options: a: Rectangle, b: Square, c: Octagon
note: A stop sign is always an octagon. This unique eight‑sided shape helps drivers recognize the sign’s meaning quickly, even from the back or in poor visibility, so they know they must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection.

question: A steady yellow light at an intersection indicates:
options: a: Proceed, b: Yield to other vehicles, c: Slow down and prepare to stop
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, you may proceed with caution.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal indicate?
options: a: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.,b: Come to a complete stop.,c: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow left arrow means you may make the turn, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Oncoming vehicles with a green light have the right-of-way, so turn only when there is a safe gap.

question: When may you cross solid yellow lines?
options: a: To pass traffic in the same direction.,b: Only when making a left turn.,c: At any time.
note: A solid yellow line generally means you may not pass. However, you may cross a solid yellow line when making a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or intersection, but only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?
options: a: Proceed only after coming to a complete stop and yielding to any crossing traffic.,b: Continue without stopping because you have the right-of-way.,c: Stop only if a police officer is present.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any pedestrians and crossing traffic, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Highway markings:
options: a: Are usually unimportant, b: Are only in construction zones, c: Provide information for drivers
note: Highway markings are important visual guides that help drivers stay in the correct lane, know when it is safe or unsafe to pass, and anticipate changes such as merges, turns, or lane endings. They work together with signs and signals to keep traffic organized and safe.

question: What should you do at an unmarked railroad crossing?
options: a: Always stop completely.,b: Slow down and be ready to stop.,c: All crossings have signals, so this doesn’t apply.
note: At an unmarked railroad crossing with no lights or gates, you must slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching. Not all crossings have signals, so you cannot assume the tracks are clear.

question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with a crossbuck but no gates or lights?
options: a: Cross cautiously when no train is coming.,b: Turn down your radio to hear trains.,c: Wait for a flagger’s clearance.
note: A crossbuck without gates or lights marks a railroad crossing where you must use extra caution. Slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and only cross when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: Downward-facing triangular signs:
options: a: Indicate school zones, b: Instruct drivers to yield, c: Mark construction zones
note: A downward-facing triangle is the YIELD sign. It tells you to slow down, be prepared to stop, and let other vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians go first if they have the right-of-way.

question: You may drive around railroad crossing gates:
options: a: After the train passes, b: Never, c: When lights stop flashing
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. Lowered gates and flashing signals mean a train is approaching, and trains cannot stop quickly. You must wait until the gates are fully raised and the signals indicate it is safe before crossing.

question: An End school zone sign indicates:
options: a: A 20 mph speed limit, b: The end of a reduced speed school zone, c: A higher likelihood of pedestrians
note: An End School Zone" sign tells you that the special reduced school-zone speed limit no longer applies and you may resume the regular posted speed if conditions allow. However
difficulty: children and pedestrians may still be present near schools

question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:
options: a: Yield to traffic and pedestrians, b: Look both ways while crossing, c: Come to a complete stop
note: A red and white triangular sign is a yield sign. When you see this sign, slow down and be ready to stop. Yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Where should you stop at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a: No stop is required.,b: Slow down to check for traffic.,c: Stop at the point nearest the intersection where you can see approaching traffic without entering the roadway.
note: At a stop sign with no marked stop line or crosswalk, you must still stop. Stop at the point nearest the intersection where you can see approaching traffic on the intersecting roadway, but before entering the intersection. This usually means stopping where you can see well down the cross street in both directions.

question: What should you do at a steady red traffic light?
options: a: Come to a complete stop.,b: Continue as you have the right-of-way.,c: Stop only if a police officer is present.
note: A steady red light always means stop before the crosswalk or stop line. You must remain stopped until the light turns green, unless you are allowed to make a right turn on red (or left from a one‑way to a one‑way) after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a: Stop completely and proceed when safe, b: Turn right or left, c: Stop and wait for a green light
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as:
options: a: A solid red light, b: A stop sign, c: A yield sign
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe, yielding to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way.

question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:
options: a: Look both ways before crossing tracks, b: Obey all traffic signals, c: Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists, d: All of the above
note: At light rail intersections, you must obey all traffic signals and signs, look carefully in both directions for approaching trains, and watch for and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who may be crossing near the tracks.

question: A diamond-shaped sign:
options: a: Signals potential or existing road hazards, b: Indicates school zones, c: Marks public recreation areas
note: Diamond‑shaped signs are warning signs. They are usually yellow or orange and alert you to potential or existing hazards such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or road work ahead so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: A diamond-shaped sign represents a:
options: a: Road hazard warning, b: Interstate route marker, c: School crossing indicator
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They are usually yellow (or orange in work zones) and alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, merging traffic, or road work.

question: A single broken white line between lanes indicates:
options: a: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited, b: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed if safe, c: Traffic moves in the same direction and lane changes are allowed when safe
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and you may change lanes or pass when it is safe. On a two‑lane road with traffic moving in opposite directions, the center line is yellow, not white. A broken yellow center line means passing is allowed when you can see far enough ahead and it is safe.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a: Merging traffic ahead.,b: Proceed cautiously.,c: Pedestrian crossing nearby.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles if needed.

question: If a pedestrian hybrid beacon flashes red, it means:
options: a: Proceed with caution, b: Slow down and prepare to stop, c: Stop completely and proceed if clear
note: A flashing red on a pedestrian hybrid beacon works like a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, then proceed only when the crosswalk is clear of pedestrians and other traffic.

question: What does a traffic signal ahead sign mean?
options: a: There is a traffic signal ahead; be prepared to slow and obey it., b: The signal ahead is malfunctioning., c: The signal ahead is green.
note: A traffic signal ahead sign warns that there is a traffic light at the upcoming intersection. It does not tell you whether the light will be red, yellow, or green when you arrive; it only alerts you to be prepared to slow down and obey the signal.

question: When can you proceed through a yellow light intersection?
options: a: If you are already in the intersection and can clear it safely.,b: If pedestrians are crossing.,c: If you're turning right.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through carefully and clear the intersection. If you have not yet entered and can safely stop, you must stop rather than speed up to beat the red. You never proceed just because an emergency vehicle or pedestrians are crossing; in those cases you must yield.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal indicate?
options: a: Merge into the arrow’s lane.,b: Slow to a stop if safe.,c: Turn left after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected movement for that arrow is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection; do not stop in the middle.

question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
options: a: A fluorescent orange triangle with a red reflective border, mounted on the rear of slow‑moving vehicles; b: A green circular sign; c: A yellow diamond-shaped sign
note: A slow‑moving vehicle emblem is a fluorescent orange triangle with a red reflective border, mounted on the rear of vehicles that typically travel 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or horse‑drawn buggies. It is not a rectangular, circular, or diamond‑shaped sign.

question: Work zone signs indicate:
options: a: It’s summer, b: Stop and back up, c: Less than ideal driving conditions
note: Orange work zone signs warn that road work or maintenance is taking place and that conditions may be less predictable than normal. Drivers should slow down, be prepared for lane shifts, workers, equipment, and sudden stops, and follow any posted reduced speed limits.

question: A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle’s rear indicates:
options: a: A slow-moving vehicle, b: An ambulance, c: A school bus
note: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle is the slow‑moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, such as farm machinery or horse‑drawn vehicles, so other drivers should slow down and pass only when safe.

question: Certain highway signs mandate that drivers follow specific instructions. These are called:
options: a: Regulatory signs, b: Warning signs, c: Information signs
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way directions. They are enforceable by law, and failing to obey them can result in citations or other penalties.

question: A red arrow on a traffic light indicates:
options: a: Proceed slowly through the intersection, b: Stop and proceed when clear, c: Stop until a green light or arrow appears
note: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and you are not allowed to proceed in the direction of the arrow until it turns green or a green arrow appears. In many states, turning on a red arrow is specifically prohibited unless a sign clearly allows it, so you should remain stopped and wait for a green signal.

question: What should you do when approaching a flashing yellow light?
options: a: Speed up to clear the intersection.,b: Stop completely.,c: Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not need to stop unless needed for traffic or pedestrians, but you must not speed up. Speeding up at a flashing yellow increases crash risk because it usually marks a higher‑risk area such as an intersection or pedestrian crossing.

question: An octagonal sign is always a:
options: a: Speed limit sign, b: Stop sign, c: Hospital sign
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign shape is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see an octagonal sign, you must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a: May still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic, b: Must go straight, c: Retain the right-of-way to turn
note: When a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you may still turn in the same direction, but you no longer have a protected turn. You must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Make the turn only when it is safe and there is a sufficient gap in oncoming traffic.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash over a symbol means:
options: a: Drivers must stop completely, b: The action is prohibited, c: Some drivers must yield
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol is a regulatory sign that means you may not do the action shown. For example, a right‑turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no right turn is allowed.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:
options: a: Stop fully and proceed when safe, b: Stop only if other cars approach, c: Stop only if cars are in the intersection
note: At a flashing red light, you must make a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you yield to any traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way, then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate being raised or lowered?
options: a: If the train isn't too close.,b: No, you must stop.,c: If you look both ways.
note: You may never drive around or under a railroad crossing gate while it is being lowered or raised. You must stop and remain stopped until the lights and bells stop and the gate is fully raised, and you have checked that no train is coming.

question: What should you do at a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a: Speed up to avoid stopping.,b: Continue as you have the right-of-way.,c: Slow to a stop unless already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, continue through with caution.

question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a: Stop and wait for the light to change.,b: Make a U-turn as the intersection is closed.,c: Proceed carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down as needed, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and be prepared to yield if necessary.

question: What does a green arrow lane control signal above a reversible lane signify?
options: a: The lane is open for travel in the direction of the arrow.,b: Drivers should avoid this lane.,c: Drivers may only use this lane for left turns.
note: A green arrow over a lane means that lane is open for travel in the direction of the arrow. In reversible lanes, a green arrow allows you to use that lane; a red X means you must not drive in that lane.

question: What should you do when nearing a railroad crossing warning sign?
options: a: Drive faster than the train.,b: Be ready to stop if a train is near.,c: Find a way around lowered gates.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must be prepared to stop. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop if a train is approaching or if signals or gates are activated. Never try to beat a train or go around lowered gates.

question: A speed restriction sign:
options: a: Can be ignored in adverse weather, b: Is rectangular with a black number on a yellow background, c: Is blue with black lettering
note: Advisory speed plaques used with curve or turn warning signs are rectangular with a black number on a yellow background. They show a recommended safe speed for that specific condition, especially useful in bad weather or on sharp curves. They are not triangular and are not blue.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that a ____ light will soon appear.
options: a: Flashing yellow, b: Steady green, c: Steady red
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must slow down and stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. It is a warning that the green phase is ending and a steady red light will appear next.

question: What should you do when nearing railroad tracks?
options: a: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.,b: Speed up to cross before gates lower.,c: Drive around a lowered gate.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, you should always look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Never speed up to beat a train and never drive around or under a lowered gate; trains cannot stop quickly and a collision is often fatal.

question: When turning onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line, you know:
options: a: It’s a two-way road, b: It’s a one-way road, c: The road is under repair
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on a two-lane road means it is a two-way road and passing is allowed when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited. One-way roads typically use white lane lines, not yellow, between lanes going in the same direction.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line signifies:
options: a: Passing is allowed from either direction, b: Passing is permitted from the lane adjacent to the broken line, c: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for drivers in the lane next to the broken line, and only when it is safe. Drivers in the lane next to the solid line may not cross it to pass.

question: When stopped at a stop sign in a line of vehicles with no cross traffic after others pass, you:
options: a: Proceed without stopping again, b: Stop again at the stop sign or line, c: Roll past the stop sign slowly
note: At a stop sign, every vehicle must make its own complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Even if the car ahead of you has already stopped and gone, you must stop again at the proper place before proceeding.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a: It’s summer.,b: Stop and back up immediately.,c: Less than ideal driving conditions.
note: Orange work zone signs warn that road work is taking place and that normal conditions may be changed. Lanes may narrow, traffic may slow or stop unexpectedly, and workers or equipment may be close to traffic. Drivers must slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for less than ideal driving conditions.

question: A flashing red light at a traffic signal means:
options: a: The same as a stop sign, b: The signal is malfunctioning, c: No complete stop is required
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line or before the crosswalk, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield as required, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: A flashing red traffic signal is equivalent to:
options: a: A slow sign, b: A yield sign, c: A stop sign
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe and you have yielded the right‑of‑way where required.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a: It’s illegal to go around lowered gates, b: You must stop when a flagger directs, c: Not all crossings have flashing signals or gates, d: All of the above
note: It is illegal to drive around or through lowered railroad gates, you must always obey a flagger’s directions, and many railroad crossings do not have flashing lights or gates. Because all three statements are true, “All of the above” is correct.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:
options: a: Drivers in that lane may choose to follow the arrow, b: Drivers must follow the arrow only if traffic lights are off, c: Drivers in that lane must follow the arrow
note: Pavement arrows show the direction(s) traffic in that lane must go. If you are in a lane with a straight arrow, you must go straight; with a left-turn arrow, you must turn left, unless a sign or signal specifically allows another movement.

question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slanting left indicates:
options: a: The road or shoulder narrows ahead, b: A construction zone is approaching, c: A left turn is required soon
note: A solid white line along the right edge of the road is an edge line. When it angles or slants toward the center of the road, it usually indicates that the roadway is narrowing or the shoulder is ending, so you should prepare to adjust your lane position and use extra caution. It does not mean a left turn is required.

question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a: To pass a slow truck.,b: To turn into a driveway.,c: To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and generally may not be crossed to pass. You may only cross them to make a left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a permitted U-turn when it is safe.

question: What does a stop sign indicate?
options: a: Slow down and prepare to stop if vehicles approach.,b: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,c: Image of a stop sign.
note: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as required, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: When can you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a: After slowing to check for traffic.,b: After stopping and verifying safety.,c: After stopping 20 feet before the intersection.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, usually at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic. After stopping and confirming it is safe, you may proceed.

question: You must stop at an intersection for a:
options: a: Flashing red light, b: Steady yellow light, c: Yellow arrow
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when it is safe and the way is clear. A steady yellow or yellow arrow is a warning that the signal is about to turn red; you should prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a: Stop and proceed when safe.,b: Stop only if other cars approach.,c: Stop only if cars are in the intersection.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: What should you do at an intersection with a solid yellow light?
options: a: Proceed through the intersection without slowing.,b: Stop immediately, even if you must brake hard.,c: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely; if you cannot stop safely, proceed with caution.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to the intersection to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than braking hard and risking a rear‑end collision.

question: Double solid yellow lines in the middle of a road indicate:
options: a: Railroad crossing ahead, b: Pedestrian crossing ahead, c: No passing from either direction (except for permitted left turns across the lines when safe)
note: Double solid yellow lines mean vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when directed by traffic control, but not to pass moving vehicles.

question: A solid white line in the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited, b: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed if safe, c: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited
note: A solid white line is used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and generally discourages or prohibits lane changes where it is painted. Center lines between traffic moving in opposite directions are yellow, not white.

question: What should you do at a steady green traffic light?
options: a: Proceed unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.,b: Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c: Treat it as a four-way stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn if it is safe, but you must yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection and to oncoming traffic when turning left.

question: Diagonal stripes sloping downward to the right on a barricade mean:
options: a: Stop, b: Bear to the right, c: Bear to the left
note: On barricades and object markers, the diagonal stripes show which side you should pass on. If the stripes slope downward to the right, you must pass to the right of the barricade; if they slope downward to the left, you pass to the left.

question: Where should you stop at a stop line?
options: a: Before the stop line.,b: On the stop line.,c: Past the stop line.
note: You must stop before the stop line so that your vehicle does not enter the crosswalk or intersection. The stop line marks where you must stop to keep pedestrians safe and to maintain a clear view of cross traffic and signals.

question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes mean?
options: a: Passing is allowed if safe.,b: Both lanes move in the same direction.,c: Passing is prohibited.
note: A single dashed yellow line between lanes means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it can be done safely. You may cross the line to pass, but only when you have enough clear distance and will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a: Reduce speed, b: Pass with caution, c: Do not pass
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may not pass other vehicles. It marks a no‑passing zone because sight distance or other conditions make passing unsafe, so you must stay in your lane until the line pattern changes and it is safe and legal to pass.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a: If a stop sign is posted., b: If a gate is lowered., c: If crossing lights are flashing., d: All of the above.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time warning devices indicate a train is coming or when signs or officials require it. This includes when red lights are flashing, when the gate is lowered or is being lowered, when a stop sign is posted, when a flagger signals you to stop, or when you can see or hear an approaching train.

question: If traffic signals fail due to a power outage:
options: a: Park off the road and wait, b: Use hand signals, c: Turn on hazard lights and proceed, d: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when safe
note: When a traffic signal is not working because of a power outage, you must treat the intersection as a four‑way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn, yielding to any vehicles already in the intersection and to pedestrians. You do not park and wait, and you do not simply turn on hazard lights and go through.

question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with flashing signals?
options: a: Stop and look for a train.,b: Slow down and look for a train.,c: Look for a train and speed up.
note: Flashing signals at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop before the tracks, typically no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail, look and listen for trains in both directions, and remain stopped until the signals stop and it is clearly safe to proceed.

question: What does a steady green arrow at a traffic signal mean?
options: a: Merge into the arrow’s lane.,b: Slow to a stop if safe.,c: Turn in the arrow’s direction after yielding.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed to turn, but you must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection. Use the arrow as your signal that cross traffic is stopped by a red light, but always check the intersection before completing the turn.

question: When must you stop at an intersection?
options: a: At a flashing red light.,b: At a steady yellow light.,c: At a yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go. A steady yellow or yellow arrow is a warning that the light is about to change and you should prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

question: What do large flashing arrow signs indicate?
options: a: Drivers should merge into the lane the arrow points to.,b: There is something to observe in the arrow's direction.,c: Drivers can remain in their current lane.
note: Large flashing or sequential arrow panels in work zones warn that a lane is closed ahead and direct drivers to move safely into the lane indicated by the arrow. You should slow down and merge into the lane the arrow points to.

question: Coming to a full stop at an intersection, yielding to traffic/pedestrians, and proceeding when clear corresponds to:
options: a: A flashing red light, b: A flashing yellow light, c: A solid green light
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. You must then yield to any traffic and pedestrians in or approaching the intersection and proceed only when it is safe. A solid red light requires a stop but does not flash; a flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution without stopping if the way is clear.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:
options: a: Warns of road conditions or hazards, b: Guides to nearby cities and towns, c: Indicates traffic laws
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to upcoming road conditions or hazards such as curves, intersections, animal crossings, or changes in road surface so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?
options: a: At any time.,b: Only during daylight.,c: When safe to change lanes.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it when you are changing lanes or passing, but only after checking mirrors and blind spots and ensuring there is enough space to move safely without interfering with other traffic.

question: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited, b: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed if safe, c: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited
note: A double solid yellow line means traffic is moving in opposite directions and neither side may cross the lines to pass. You may only cross to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road where it is specifically allowed, but not to overtake another vehicle.

question: At a railroad crossing with a crossbuck but no gates or lights, you should:
options: a: Cross cautiously only when no train is coming, b: Turn down your radio to listen for a train, c: Proceed only when cleared by a flagger, d: All of the above
note: A crossbuck marks a railroad crossing. At a crossing without gates or lights, you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and only cross when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks. Turning down the radio and obeying a flagger are good practices when needed, but the key legal requirement is to yield to any train and cross only when it is clearly safe.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection indicates:
options: a: Slow down and proceed cautiously, b: Continue through normally, c: Stop and wait for a green light
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, look for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe.

question: Guide signs are ____ signs providing directional and mileage information.
options: a: Yellow, b: Red, c: Green
note: Guide signs are green signs that give you directions, route information, and distances to cities, exits, and points of interest. Their purpose is to help you navigate and plan lane changes or turns in advance while driving.

question: A yellow light flashing on and off means:
options: a: Slow down, check for traffic, and proceed with caution, b: Stop and wait for a green light, c: Speed up to clear the intersection
note: A flashing yellow light indicates caution, requiring drivers to slow down, check for traffic, and proceed when safe.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a: Stop at the stop line, b: Stop before entering a crosswalk, c: Stop before entering the intersection, d: All of the above
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line, stop there; if not, stop before the crosswalk; if neither is present, stop before entering the intersection. This ensures you do not block pedestrians or cross traffic.

question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when clear.,b: Turn right or left only if directed by signs or markings.,c: Stop and remain stopped until the light stops flashing.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe and clear.

question: Can you drive around railroad crossing gates?
options: a: After the train passes., b: Never., c: When lights stop flashing.
note: Never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised, then look and listen for any additional trains before crossing.

question: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you should:
options: a: Stop and proceed only after the lights stop and you are sure no train is coming., b: Slow down and look for a train, c: Look for a train and speed up
note: Flashing lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must come to a complete stop before the tracks and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and you are sure no train is coming. Never try to beat the train or go around lowered gates.

question: What does a railroad crossing sign indicate?
options: a: A train station is ahead.,b: Signal before proceeding.,c: Slow down and yield to trains.
note: A railroad crossing sign warns that train tracks are ahead. You must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Always yield the right-of-way to any approaching train, as trains cannot stop quickly.

question: What does a steady yellow X lane control signal above a reversible lane mean?
options: a: The signal will soon change to a red X.,b: The signal will soon change to a green arrow.,c: Drivers can continue in this lane.
note: A steady yellow X over a reversible lane means the lane is about to close to traffic in your direction. You should safely move out of that lane because the signal will soon change to a red X, which means you may not drive in that lane.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:
options: a: Drive straight ahead only, b: Drive only in the direction of the green arrow, c: Wait for a solid green light to proceed
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, even if the main signal is red. You may proceed only in the direction of the arrow and must still yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What should you do when moving from the left lane to the right on a multilane highway?
options: a: Check rearview mirror before changing lanes.,b: Look over your right shoulder for blind spots after signaling and checking mirrors.,c: Check side mirror and signal.
note: Before moving from the left lane to the right, signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your right shoulder to check your blind spot. Turning your head lets you see areas your mirrors cannot, helping you avoid vehicles that may be hidden beside you.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a: Sound your horn, b: Turn on your headlights, c: Check your mirrors and blind spots
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors and prevents sideswipe collisions.

question: You should always signal when:
options: a: Changing lanes, b: Pulling into or out of a parking space, c: Entering traffic from an alley or parking area, d: All of the above
note: You must signal any time you change direction or move your vehicle laterally, including changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, and entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling clearly tells other road users what you intend to do and helps prevent collisions.

question: Do not pass:
options: a: On hills or curves, b: When school bus lights are flashing, c: Near intersections, d: All of the above
note: Passing is unsafe and often illegal when you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on hills or curves; when a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, because children may be crossing; and near or within intersections, where vehicles, pedestrians, and turning traffic create additional hazards. In these situations, you must not pass.

question: You may pass another vehicle:
options: a: In a curve or on a hill, b: Using the shoulder, c: If your lane is next to a broken yellow line and the passing lane is clear
note: You may pass another vehicle only when it is legal and safe. A solid yellow line on your side of the road means passing is prohibited, even if the lane next to you has a broken line. Never pass on hills, curves, or using the shoulder, because your view and space are limited and you may not see oncoming traffic in time.

question: How far in advance should you signal a turn?
options: a: 100 feet.,b: 50 feet.,c: 20 feet.
note: You should signal at least 100 feet before turning so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians have enough time to see your signal and react safely.

question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a: In a curve or on a hill., b: On the shoulder., c: If your lane is next to a broken yellow line.
note: You may only pass when there is a broken (dashed) line on your side of the center and it is safe to do so. You must not pass on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, you must not pass on the shoulder, and you must not cross a solid yellow line on your side of the road.

question: You should signal to turn ____ before beginning the turn.
options: a: 100 feet, b: 50 feet, c: 20 feet
note: You should signal at least 100 feet before turning so other road users have enough time to see your signal and react. At higher speeds, signal even earlier to give extra warning.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
options: a: Mixed solid and broken yellow, b: Single broken yellow, c: Double solid yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the line to pass. This marking is used where sight distance is limited or passing would be especially dangerous. A single broken yellow line allows passing when it is safe, and a mixed solid and broken yellow line allows passing only for traffic on the side with the broken line.

question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a: Signal your intent only.,b: Check your mirrors only.,c: Signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.
note: A safe lane change on a highway requires all three actions together: signal well in advance to communicate your intention, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Relying on only one of these steps is unsafe because vehicles can be hidden in areas your mirrors do not show.

question: When waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection with blocked visibility, you should:
options: a: Accelerate when the first lane is clear, b: Wait until all lanes are clear, c: Proceed if an oncoming driver waves you through
note: At a multilane intersection with limited visibility, you must wait until all lanes you need to cross or enter are clear before turning left. Never rely on another driver waving you through, and do not move just because one lane is open if others may still have oncoming traffic.

question: When using a hand signal for a turn, stop signaling:
options: a: Mid-turn, b: After completing the turn, c: Just before the turn
note: Hand signals are used when your turn signals don’t work or are hard to see. You signal well before the turn so others know your intention, then stop signaling just before you turn so you can keep both hands on the wheel and maintain full control through the turn.

question: When may you pass a vehicle on the right shoulder?
options: a: Never on the shoulder; you may not use the shoulder as a travel lane to pass.,b: When the vehicle ahead is too slow.,c: When the vehicle ahead is turning.
note: You must not drive onto or use the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is not a travel lane and is meant for emergencies or breakdowns, not passing. Passing on the right is only allowed when it can be done safely within a proper lane, never by driving off the roadway or onto the shoulder.

question: You cannot safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street unless:
options: a: The road ahead is clearly visible, b: You can return to your lane before oncoming traffic, c: Your vehicle can achieve the necessary speed, d: All of the above
note: Passing on a two-way, two-lane road is only safe when you can clearly see far enough ahead, your vehicle can accelerate and pass without lingering in the oncoming lane, and you can return to your lane before any oncoming traffic reaches you. All of these conditions must be met before you begin to pass.

question: When should you stop using a hand signal for a turn?
options: a: During the turn.,b: After the turn.,c: Just before the turn.
note: When using hand and arm signals, you should signal for at least the last 100 feet before turning, then return your hand to the steering wheel as you begin and complete the turn so you can keep proper control of the vehicle.

question: To turn left at an intersection with a green light but heavy oncoming traffic, you should:
options: a: Use the next intersection.,b: Wait at the crosswalk.,c: Wait in the intersection.
note: With a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you should pull into the intersection when it is legal to do so, keep your wheels straight, and wait there until there is a safe gap to turn left. When the light turns yellow or red, you must clear the intersection by completing your turn if it is safe. Simply skipping the intersection is not the standard or required action.

question: When can you not pass safely on a two-way, two-lane road?
options: a: When you cannot clearly see enough clear road ahead.,b: When you cannot return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c: When your vehicle cannot reach the needed speed to pass safely.
note: You may only pass on a two-way, two-lane road when all safety conditions are met: you can clearly see enough clear road ahead, you can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can accelerate fast enough to pass without forcing others to slow or swerve. If your vehicle cannot reach the needed speed, it is not safe to pass.

question: How should you pass another vehicle on a two-lane road?
options: a: Return to your lane when there’s enough space.,b: Stay in the left lane if turning left.,c: Return to the right side immediately.
note: On a two-lane road, pass only when it is legal and safe, then return to your lane after you can see enough clear space between you and the vehicle you passed. Do not cut back in too soon, and do not remain in the oncoming lane longer than necessary.

question: What must you do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a: Always signal, even with no traffic.,b: Signal only if traffic is visible.,c: Signal only at night.
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if you think no one else is around. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do so they can react safely and avoid collisions.

question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:
options: a: If it interferes with traffic, b: When turning left into a driveway, c: If the car ahead is disabled
note: A single broken white or yellow line means you may cross it to change lanes or pass, but only when it is safe and will not interfere with other traffic. You must not move into another lane or across the line if doing so forces other drivers to slow or swerve suddenly.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the dividing line is:
options: a: A broken white line, b: Double solid yellow, c: Solid yellow
note: A broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and allows lane changes and passing when it is safe. Solid yellow lines and double solid yellow lines generally mean you may not pass because they separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mark no-passing zones.

question: When a road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:
options: a: Only in an emergency, b: If on an expressway, c: If traffic is clear
note: A solid yellow line with a broken yellow line means passing is allowed only on the side with the broken line. If the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass when there is no oncoming traffic and you can complete the pass safely.

question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:
options: a: To pass a slow truck, b: To turn into a driveway, c: To pass another car
note: Double solid yellow lines mean you may not cross them to pass another vehicle. However, you are allowed to cross them to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make a legal U-turn where permitted. Passing across double solid yellow lines is unsafe and illegal in standard U.S. rules.

question: When changing lanes, it’s important to:
options: a: Signal your intentions, b: Check your blind spot, c: Ensure the lane is clear, d: All of the above
note: Before changing lanes, always signal to let others know your intentions, check your mirrors and blind spot to see vehicles you cannot see directly in the mirrors, and make sure the lane is clear and there is enough space to move safely.

question: What should you do when passing on a multilane highway?
options: a: Ensure the passing lane is clear.,b: Pass only on the right.,c: Watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction.
note: On a multilane highway, you normally pass on the left and must first make sure the lane you will move into is clear, then signal and change lanes smoothly. You do not watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction because traffic in your direction is separated by lanes or a median.

question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a: Always signal, even with no visible traffic, b: Signal only if traffic is visible, c: Signal only at night
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if you do not see other vehicles, pedestrians, or cyclists. Signaling clearly and early lets others anticipate your movement and reduces the chance of collisions.

question: How close may you not pass within to a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel?
options: a: 200 feet.,b: 100 feet.,c: 500 feet.
note: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel when your view is obstructed, because you may not be able to see oncoming traffic in time to avoid a collision. This distance helps ensure you have enough clear sight and space to pass safely and legally.

question: What should you avoid when changing lanes?
options: a: Changing lanes without checking mirrors and blind spots., b: Changing lanes without signaling your intent., c: Changing lanes without checking for other drivers moving into the same lane., d: All of the above.
